# A function a test hands its `Test` asserts and waits through it as the
# test body does, on a placed program in C and Go, on win32 and gtk4: the
# helper is written with the tests, its `t` the agent's test, where C wrote
# win32's Go wait loop into it, or refused its `t.assert`, and Go had no
# implementation of `t.assert`. A helper's failure fails the test calling it.

! sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c app.sngl
stdout '--- PASS: /AHelperPasses'
stdout '--- FAIL: /AHelperFails'
stdout '2 tests, 1 failures'

! sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '--- PASS: /AHelperPasses'
stdout '--- FAIL: /AHelperFails'
stdout '2 tests, 1 failures'

[!gtk4] skip 'gtk4 needs its development libraries to build'

! sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c app.sngl
stdout '--- PASS: /AHelperPasses'
stdout '--- FAIL: /AHelperFails'
stdout '2 tests, 1 failures'

! sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '--- PASS: /AHelperPasses'
stdout '--- FAIL: /AHelperFails'
stdout '2 tests, 1 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component counter ui.node {
    var hits = 0

    ui.button #b(text="{hits}", @click { hits += 1 })
}

var asked = 0

func atLeast(t test.Test, got int, want int) {
    t.assert(got >= want)
}

func settle(t test.Test) {
    asked = 0
    t.wait(
        func() bool {
            asked += 1
            return asked > 2
        },
        2000,
    )
    t.assert(asked == 3)
}

func testAHelperPasses(t test.Test, c counter) {
    c.b.click()
    settle(t)
    atLeast(t, c.hits, 1)
}

func testAHelperFails(t test.Test, c counter) {
    atLeast(t, c.hits, 1)
}

ui.window {
    counter
}
